shared.requirement: Continue in the PS3 repository and clearly mark where PS4 starts in analyses/ps3_script.py. Provide a reproducible entry point for the submitted exercise.
Use the team's fixed IDpol split, ClaimAmountCut / Exposure target, and Exposure weights wherever applicable. Use Tweedie power 1.5 for the team's deviance comparisons.

requirements.requirement: Plot average claims by BonusMalus group using Exposure weights and explain what can happen without an explicit constraint.
Name the new pipeline or estimator constrained_lgbm. After preprocessing, use a constraint vector matching the actual feature order, with +1 for BonusMalus and 0 elsewhere.
Cross-validate on training folds, select the best constrained estimator, and predict using that estimator. The held-out test sample must not affect parameter selection.
Compare prediction accuracy with the unconstrained LGBM on a common split and criterion; interpret the comparison consistently with the evidence.
Generate held-out predictions as pp_t_lgbm_constrained and align them by IDpol for downstream exercises.
Refit the constrained LightGBM with the best cross-validated parameters from Ex1, keeping the BonusMalus constraint.
Pass both training and test datasets through eval_set, using the fitted training preprocessing and corresponding Exposure weights. Keep the test curves out of parameter selection.
Use lgb.plot_metric to show the training and test metric over boosting iterations and interpret convergence, overfitting and whether the chosen configuration looks well tuned.
Define evaluate_predictions in evaluation/_evaluate_predictions.py, export it from the evaluation package, and accept actual outcomes, predictions and sample weights.
Compute bias relative to the actual exposure-adjusted mean, weighted deviance, weighted MAE and weighted RMSE. Return a DataFrame indexed by metric name.
Use the function to compare constrained and unconstrained LightGBM on matched policies and weights. Gini is optional and follows the PS3 Lorenz definition if included.
Use DALEX Explainer with fitted constrained and unconstrained LightGBM estimators or pipelines, and compatible model inputs.
Compute partial dependence via DALEX model_profile for all modelling features, and plot and compare both models on comparable backgrounds and grids.
Create DALEX explainers for the initial GLM and constrained LightGBM using comparable background data and explain the same selected test policy.
Call predict_parts with type='shap' for both models and plot both decompositions.
Compare how the decompositions and feature contributions differ for that policy, consistent with the reported plots and predictions.
